elements.element: The renewal mechanism must be either renewal only by mutual written agreement or automatic renewal.
elements.evidence: The clause expressly provides for automatic renewal.

elements.element: If renewal is automatic rather than solely by mutual written agreement, each renewal term must be 12 months.
elements.evidence: Each automatic renewal is for an additional one-year period.

elements.element: If renewal is automatic rather than solely by mutual written agreement, Customer must be able to opt out on 30 days' written notice.
elements.evidence: Assuming Company is Customer, the agreement renews automatically unless Company terminates on 30 days' written notice. This permits Company to prevent renewal by giving timely notice.

elements.element: If renewal is automatic rather than solely by mutual written agreement, Vendor must remind Customer 60 days before each renewal.
elements.evidence: The operative clause contains no reminder obligation for HDI and no 60-day reminder trigger.

elements.element: Any price increase must be capped at the lesser of CPI and 3%.
elements.evidence: The clause contains no price-increase cap or CPI-based limitation.

elements.element: If the agreement renews automatically, Customer's required non-renewal notice period must be no more than 60 days.
elements.evidence: Assuming Company is Customer, Company may prevent renewal through 30 days' written termination notice, which is within the 60-day maximum.

elements.element: Any price increase must be capped at 5%.
elements.evidence: The clause contains no price-increase cap.

result.reason: The redline improves Customer's notice period to 30 days but omits both the Vendor reminder and every price-increase limitation. It therefore reaches neither the preferred nor fallback position. Although the edit is narrow and leaves unrelated terms intact, it is not minimal as defined because it does not achieve a complete acceptable level.
